newsitem.title: USA: August U.S. light vehicle sales fall 2.3 percent.
newsitem.headline: August U.S. light vehicle sales fall 2.3 percent.

text.p: U.S. car and light truck sales during the month of August totaled 1,307,858 units with all automakers reporting, a 2.3 percent decline on a daily selling basis from the 1,338,278 units sold a year earlier.

The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for the month was 15.8 million units, up from 15.7 million units a year earlier and 14.3 million units for the month of July. The rate is calculated with seasonal factors supplied by the U.S. Commerce Department.
Automakers sold 608,140 North American-built cars in the United States in August, down 6.7 percent from a year ago.
The seasonally adjusted annual rate for domestic cars was 7.42 million units, compared with 6.83 million in July and 7.75 in August 1995.

Automakers sold 513,376 domestic trucks in the United States during August, up 3.7 percent from a year earlier. The seasonally adjusted annual sales rate for domestic trucks was 6.51 million units, compared with 5.94 million a year earlier and 5.77 million in July.
Truck numbers include medium-duty truck sales from General Motors Corp. GM on Thursday did not provide a separate list of light truck sales, as it normally does.

Imported car sales totaled 141,744 units, down 8.3 percent from a year ago, with a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.42 million units. Imported truck sales rose 21.3 percent to 44,598 units for an annual rate of 450,000 units.
